atoms.text: This guide configures the destination bucket dr-invoices-west to receive objects replicated from invoices-east by the VaultSync replication feature. The destination bucket policy contains one Allow statement that covers replication writes only. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/vaultsync-replication-role, which is created in the source account and assumed by the replication job. The Action list contains s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner. The Resource element is arn:aws:s3:::dr-invoices-west/*, so the role can write only object-level data into the bucket. Before you save the policy, confirm that the role's own IAM permissions policy allows reading from the source bucket. The role must also carry a trust policy that lets the replication job assume it. After you apply the policy, enable versioning on both buckets and create a replication rule that sends every new object under the invoices/ prefix to the destination.

This guide configures the destination bucket dr-invoices-west to receive objects replicated from invoices-east by the VaultSync replication feature. The destination bucket policy contains one Allow statement that covers replication writes only. The Principal is the service principal vaultsync.example-cloud.com, so the replication job writes under the service's own identity and no role needs to be created. The Action list contains s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner. The Resource element is arn:aws:s3:::dr-invoices-west/*, so the service can write only object-level data into the bucket. Add a Condition block with aws:SourceAccount set to 111122223333 and aws:SourceArn set to the ARN of the source bucket, so that only replication from invoices-east is accepted. After you apply the policy, enable versioning on both buckets. Then create a replication rule that sends every new object under the invoices/ prefix to the destination.

This procedure grants a nightly database snapshot export job write access to the bucket db-snapshots-archive. The SnapChain backup scheduler starts the export at 02:00 UTC and uploads compressed snapshot files under the prefix nightly/. The bucket policy has one Allow statement for the upload path. Its Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/snapchain-export-role, which the export job assumes in the account that owns the database. The statement allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::db-snapshots-archive/nightly/*. A Condition requires s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms, so unencrypted uploads are rejected. The role's trust policy must permit the scheduler to assume it, and the KMS key policy must allow the role to generate data keys. After the first run, verify that the snapshot objects appear under nightly/ with the expected size and encryption metadata.

This procedure grants a nightly database snapshot export job write access to the bucket db-snapshots-archive. The SnapChain backup scheduler starts the export at 02:00 UTC and uploads compressed snapshot files under the prefix nightly/. The bucket policy has one Allow statement for the upload path. Its Principal is the service principal snapchain.example-cloud.com, which the scheduler uses when it writes on behalf of the account that owns the database. The statement allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::db-snapshots-archive/nightly/*. A Condition requires s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms, and a second Condition pins aws:SourceAccount to 444455556666 so that other accounts cannot use the same service to write here. The KMS key policy must also allow the service principal to generate data keys. After the first run, verify that the snapshot objects appear under nightly/ with the expected size and encryption metadata.

This section describes a read-only restore path from the bucket vault-cold-copies, which holds archived copies of customer exports for disaster recovery. During a recovery exercise, the ArchiveMirror restore workflow reads these objects and rehydrates them into a standby environment. The bucket policy includes a statement that permits only read operations. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/archivemirror-restore-role, located in the recovery account. The Action list is s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:ListBucket. The statement is scoped to both the bucket ARN and the object ARN pattern, because listing requires the bucket-level resource. No write or delete actions are granted, so the stored copies cannot be altered during a restore. The role's trust policy should be limited to the restore workflow, and the role should be tested with a sample object before a real recovery is needed.

This section describes a read-only restore path from the bucket vault-cold-copies, which holds archived copies of customer exports for disaster recovery. During a recovery exercise, the ArchiveMirror restore workflow reads these objects and rehydrates them into a standby environment. The bucket policy includes a statement that permits only read operations. The Principal is the service principal archivemirror.example-cloud.com, which performs the reads under its own identity. The Action list is s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:ListBucket. The statement is scoped to both the bucket ARN and the object ARN pattern, because listing requires the bucket-level resource. A Condition with aws:SourceAccount set to 777788889999 limits the service to restore workflows owned by the recovery account. No write or delete actions are granted, so the stored copies cannot be altered during a restore, and the workflow should be tested with a sample object before a real recovery is needed.

This guide sets up a compliance bucket, audit-logs-vault, that receives replicated audit logs from several member accounts for long-term retention. The LogReplica replication feature copies each log object from the member bucket to the vault bucket within minutes of creation. The vault bucket policy uses one Allow statement per member account, and this example shows the first one. The Principal is the account root arn:aws:iam::123412341234:root, which delegates the write permission to the replication role in that account through its own IAM policy. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::audit-logs-vault/member-a/*. Each member account is limited to its own prefix, so one account cannot overwrite the logs of another. Object Lock in compliance mode is enabled on the vault bucket with a retention period of 365 days. Repeat the statement for each additional member account, changing the account ID and prefix.

This guide sets up a compliance bucket, audit-logs-vault, that receives replicated audit logs from several member accounts for long-term retention. The LogReplica replication feature copies each log object from the member bucket to the vault bucket within minutes of creation. The vault bucket policy uses one Allow statement per member account, and this example shows the first one. The Principal is the service principal logreplica.example-cloud.com, which writes directly and does not rely on a role in the member account. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::audit-logs-vault/member-a/*. A Condition with aws:SourceAccount set to 123412341234 limits this statement to member A, which is also confined to its own prefix. Object Lock in compliance mode is enabled on the vault bucket with a retention period of 365 days. Repeat the statement for each additional member account, changing the account ID and prefix.

This page explains how to let an on-premises file backup gateway store incremental backups in the bucket office-files-backup. The gateway, called DepotLink, scans a file server every hour and uploads changed files under the prefix incremental/. The bucket policy has an Allow statement that covers the upload operations. Its Principal is the IAM user arn:aws:iam::202020202020:user/depotlink-uploader, whose access keys are stored in the gateway's configuration. The Action list is s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging, and s3:AbortMultipartUpload, applied to arn:aws:s3:::office-files-backup/incremental/*. A second Condition restricts requests to the corporate egress range 203.0.113.0/24 through aws:SourceIp. The user has no permissions beyond this bucket. Rotate the access keys on a fixed schedule and update the gateway whenever they change.

This page explains how to let a managed file backup gateway store incremental backups in the bucket office-files-backup. The gateway, called DepotLink, scans a file server every hour and uploads changed files under the prefix incremental/. The bucket policy has an Allow statement that covers the upload operations. Its Principal is the service principal depotlink.example-cloud.com, which signs upload requests with the service's own identity and needs no stored access keys. The Action list is s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging, and s3:AbortMultipartUpload, applied to arn:aws:s3:::office-files-backup/incremental/*. A Condition restricts requests with aws:SourceAccount set to 202020202020 and aws:SourceArn set to the ARN of the gateway resource. No other identity is granted access through this statement. There are no credentials to rotate, and the gateway needs only to be linked to the bucket by name.

This guide covers disaster recovery replication of container image archives from the bucket registry-artifacts-primary to registry-artifacts-standby. The ImageMirror feature copies layer blobs and manifest files whenever a new image tag is pushed. The standby bucket policy contains an Allow statement dedicated to the copy operation. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::303030303030:role/imagemirror-copy-role, which the copy job assumes in the primary account. The statement allows s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectVersionTagging on arn:aws:s3:::registry-artifacts-standby/blobs/* and arn:aws:s3:::registry-artifacts-standby/manifests/*. Replicated objects keep their original keys, so the standby registry can serve pulls without any path rewriting. The role needs its own permission to read from the primary bucket. Compare object counts between the two buckets after the initial sync to confirm that the copy is complete.

This guide covers disaster recovery replication of container image archives from the bucket registry-artifacts-primary to registry-artifacts-standby. The ImageMirror feature copies layer blobs and manifest files whenever a new image tag is pushed. The standby bucket policy contains an Allow statement dedicated to the copy operation. The Principal is the service principal imagemirror.example-cloud.com, which performs the copy under its own identity. The statement allows s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectVersionTagging on arn:aws:s3:::registry-artifacts-standby/blobs/* and arn:aws:s3:::registry-artifacts-standby/manifests/*. Replicated objects keep their original keys, so the standby registry can serve pulls without any path rewriting. A Condition with aws:SourceArn set to the primary bucket's ARN and aws:SourceAccount set to 303030303030 binds the statement to that one copy relationship. Compare object counts between the two buckets after the initial sync to confirm that the copy is complete.

This section configures the bucket backup-reports-central to receive manifest and completion reports from a backup service. After each run, the PlanKeeper service writes a JSON manifest that lists every protected resource and its status. The reports land under the prefix reports/ and are later read by an internal audit script. The bucket policy includes one Allow statement for report delivery. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::505050505050:role/plankeeper-report-role, which is assumed by the report delivery step of each backup plan. The Action list is s3:PutObject and s3:GetBucketLocation, and the Resource list covers the bucket and arn:aws:s3:::backup-reports-central/reports/*. A Condition requires the bucket-owner-full-control ACL on each upload, so the central account owns every report. The role's trust policy should name only the report delivery step. Confirm delivery by checking that a manifest exists after the next scheduled run.

This section configures the bucket backup-reports-central to receive manifest and completion reports from a backup service. After each run, the PlanKeeper service writes a JSON manifest that lists every protected resource and its status. The reports land under the prefix reports/ and are later read by an internal audit script. The bucket policy includes one Allow statement for report delivery. The Principal is the service principal plankeeper.example-cloud.com, which delivers reports with its own identity at the end of each backup plan. The Action list is s3:PutObject and s3:GetBucketLocation, and the Resource list covers the bucket and arn:aws:s3:::backup-reports-central/reports/*. A Condition requires the bucket-owner-full-control ACL on each upload, so the central account owns every report, and aws:SourceAccount is set to 505050505050. No other condition keys are needed beyond these two. Confirm delivery by checking that a manifest exists after the next scheduled run.

This page describes a cross-account backup copy of a media library from media-origin to the bucket media-offsite-copy in a separate recovery account. The FrameVault copy job runs weekly and writes each changed video file, preserving its key and metadata. The destination bucket policy has a single Allow statement for this job. The Principal is the AWS account ID 606060606060, written as arn:aws:iam::606060606060:root, with the account administrator delegating access to a specific IAM role through an identity policy. The Action list is s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectAcl, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads. The Resource list contains the bucket ARN and the object pattern arn:aws:s3:::media-offsite-copy/*. A Condition on s3:x-amz-acl requires bucket-owner-full-control. The delegated role should be scoped to this single bucket in its identity policy. Run the job once manually and check that the object count matches.

This page describes a cross-account backup copy of a media library from media-origin to the bucket media-offsite-copy in a separate recovery account. The FrameVault copy job runs weekly and writes each changed video file, preserving its key and metadata. The destination bucket policy has a single Allow statement for this job. The Principal is the service principal framevault.example-cloud.com, so the job writes under the service's identity and no identity policy is delegated in the source account. The Action list is s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectAcl, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads. The Resource list contains the bucket ARN and the object pattern arn:aws:s3:::media-offsite-copy/*. A Condition on s3:x-amz-acl requires bucket-owner-full-control, and a second Condition sets aws:SourceAccount to 606060606060. Run the job once manually and check that the object count matches.
